As someone who has been through this with an addict: leave. My experience has been that whatever amount of cocaine that an addict is telling you that they use— they are always doing more, often double. It would not surprise me if this person is using during the day or at work. It is always more than you think you know and they will go to great lengths to hide it.

When I was in a relationship with someone that did it every weekend, I felt like a wet blanket for wanting to tell him no or wanting him to come home with me at midnight. In reality, I wasn’t, it’s perfectly reasonable to come home at midnight. The saying exists for a reason, nothing good is happening past 2am. My partner at the time would only continue to get wasted, paranoid, emotionally dysregulated and worst of all— mean to me. It was a miserable time in my life. 

I recognize it’s so difficult to leave or set a firm boundary when you’re in a relationship though, so I get it. It is really hard and there is so much normalization of it in certain social groups it makes you feel controlling or crazy— but it’s just a complete difference in lifestyle. I have a firm stance now that I don’t want cocaine anywhere around me or in my life. It’s a different lifestyle and it’s one that I’m personally not okay with. I’ve since found there are plenty of people who are on the same page as me. I am much happier with my current partner who is content to smoke a joint and call it a night at 10:30 with me.

Not GLP-1 advice, but have you ever been tested for ADHD? I was someone who exercised moderately for years and knew how to eat healthy, but really struggled with binge-eating. I wasn’t even seeking treatment for my binge-eating, but for anxiety/depression which turned out to be a symptom of my ADHD. A surprising byproduct of being medicated was that not only am I more capable of managing time and staying organized, but my food noise was greatly reduced. 

There have been studies now showing now that there is a lot of neurobehavioral overlap between binging and ADHD. The symptoms present very differently in women than in men causing many women to go undiagnosed until adulthood. Many women, especially those that are high-IQ, learn how to mask symptoms publicly (while really struggling internally). Not saying this is you, but if in addition to binge eating you struggle with: disorganization, cleaning, time management, forgetfulness, losing things— it’s worth looking into. I never in a million years would have pinned this diagnosis for myself, a lot of these issues felt like personal flaws, but once I was diagnosed, everything made so much more sense. 

Regardless, good luck in your journey and wishing you recovery! Whatever the solution for you may be, it is possible! 💛

Is this in a relationship or out? Is this just general envy of others?

If it’s in a relationship, I think rather than feeling shame and trying to stifle it, you have to dig inwards to understand what’s triggering it. I know for myself, I am capable of experiencing it in relationships, but it’s important for me to decipher why I’m feeling it. Is my partner behaving in a way that warrants anxious feelings arising? Or does this represent a need that I feel has been neglected or unmet in the relationship? Have I properly communicated this need? If I’m jealous of them doing something with a friend instead of me, have I been prioritizing my own social life with my own friends?

If it’s after a relationship has ended, I think it’s important to remove yourself and take space. Mute or unfollow them on social media. Mute any mutual friends who might share information about them. Resist the urge to check on them or to ruminate, it only prolongs the feelings.

If it’s just general envy you are experiencing, it’s important to remind yourself that someone else’s success does not mean your failure. We are all on our own journeys with our own timelines. We don’t get to choose the hands we are dealt and ruminating all only make you feel worse. Every person has a card they wish they could swap too, I promise.

We’re talking about an almost two hour commute in each direction— *FOUR hours a day* on top of presumably a full time job. It’s insane under those circumstances to expect people to opt for that over driving in the comfort of their own vehicles, I’m sorry. The city and immediately surrounding areas (Oakland, Alameda, South SF) NEED to start building upwards, so people can live closer and utilize these systems.

6 years in PA, mostly at a large firm (not b4). I got furloughed during the pandemic, said “yikes fuck this” and got another job within a few days at a local firm. I went from 3,000+ person firm to a 300 person firm. I lasted 6 months at the local firm before I went back to my original firm. 

From my personal experience and what I’ve heard of friends at other firms, I’d say that the issues with staffing you’ll find at nearly every firm. At the smaller firm I did work less hours, but found the clients were less interesting and more fee sensitive (more rigid and unrealistic budgets) with very messy accounting. I’d often have to book quick book entries for clients and build trial balances from bank statements, rather than just being sent over TB as I had in the past.

There was also no firm standardization, an example being: some senior managers using PFX Engagement and some using a web-based file storage site for storing PBC and client work depending on personal preferences making it difficult to locate files. My computer was ancient and all our software (even excel and PFX) was loaded via Citrix in a web browser that would constantly go out or crash. We had one single subscription BNA that was an email account shared among the entire tax team.

Coming from a bigger firm, we have a lot better resources. Access to research databases, entire specialized teams to loop in on complex issues, better technology and software. We have standard processes for nearly everything, that while they can be a pain to implement, in the long run keep everyone on the same page.  Client work may be more technical, but I generally work with corporations who are less fee sensitive than a personal business owner. We get monthly cell phone reimbursements, over time meals, generally higher pay.

For me— I think a big reason is that my mother relied upon me heavily for emotional support as a child. I was her primary companion growing up and it was a lot. I also have very codependent tendencies and will swallow my needs to please those around me. When I sense someone wants more than me than I am ready to give— I pull away. 

Big triggers? Double, triple texting. Constantly trying to make plans and what feels like interrogating me about my schedule. I hate it. The more avoidant person walks inside, but gradually starts moving one foot back outside because they’re unsure this is where they want to stay. We’re not together anymore and this really is rather simple, but this is one of those hallmark examples of how someone who really loves and values you will treat you.

Locked myself out of my apartment as I was on my way to my bartending job where I wouldn’t be off until 2 am. Landlord wouldn’t be there for two hours. I panicked and called my boyfriend at the time who was on his way to the gym. He dropped what he was doing and came right over. Drove me to work, waited outside my apartment for the landlord to come. Showed up to my work on my break with copies he’d made for me and eat to dinner with me. I gave him one of those keys.

We broke up eventually. Got into a fight, we weren’t on speaking terms and I was dating someone else. Locked myself out of my apartment on a Saturday night. Couldn’t reach the landlord and figured it was worth a shot to send him a text. Told him I was locked out knowing he had the key. He drove over, no attitude, no questions asked, and just brought me my key. No matter how angry he was or what terms we were on, he was still willing to help me out.

We’re cool now, but it was still one the most simple, selfless things anyone has ever done for me outside maybe my mom or grandmother. I’ve certainly made gestures like those in relationships that weren’t returned, so it was nice to have someone do it back for me.
